newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE March Euroyen futures close down, track JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE March Euroyen futures close down, track JGBs.

text.p: Key March three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures ended down on Thursday, after spending the whole session following Japanese government bond futures in the absence of factors of their own.

Traders said many market players were on the sidelines and would likely remain so until the end of the financial half-year passes on September 30. As a result, the March contract was trapped in a narrow range of between 99.19 and 99.23.
The day's high of 99.23 was hit in the morning, when a rumour that Japan's industrial output data for August, due out on Monday, would be worse than expected.
But the trend changed by early afternoon, after key December JGB futures sank on investors' heavy selling of cash JGBs.

A modest rise in Tokyo stocks also worked to the March contract's disadvantage, some dealers added. Some long positions began to feel heavy and were unloaded, one dealer at a long-term credit bank also said.
In the interbank call market, the majority of key overnight call money was traded at 0.49 percent, unchanged from previous levels.
Wednesday was a bond settlement day, so the rate was biased downwards on Thursday, dealers said. But fund demand for the end of the financial half-year countered downward pressure.

The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) stance at its morning operation was neutral as expected. But its intention of injecting 200 billion yen, through the purchase of Treasury bills (TBs), was not fully achieved as there was only 190 billion yen worth of TBs offered.
Traders said this might have been because some market players did not have TBs to offer. But the impact of this was negligible, one trader at a city bank said.
The open market was quiet, with no benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) issued. They were offered at 0.53 percent, which was their rate on Wednesday.
About 30 billion yen worth of one-month CDs was issued at a steady 0.52 percent. Two-month CDs were offered at 0.53 percent, also steady from Wednesday's rate.
